resources.string: While an exit node carries the traffic, this network\'s own devices — a printer, a NAS, the router — are still reached directly.\n• Off: everything, the local network included, goes through the exit node.\n• Without an exit node it changes nothing.

Refuse every connection other tailnet devices open to this device, whatever the access rules allow.
• Taildrop, Taildrive, Serve, the shared proxies and this device as an exit node or relay stop answering others.
• Connections this device opens itself keep working.
• Cannot be on while Funnel is.

For organisations whose access rules check devices (posture checks).
• When the tailnet asks, the daemon sends the device's serial numbers and the MAC addresses of its network interfaces.
• On Android that is little or nothing: the serial number is given only to a device-management (MDM) app, and without root Android hides MAC addresses from apps.
• The OS and its version are reported anyway — see “Report the real OS”.

Relay traffic over UDP between tailnet devices that cannot reach each other directly, instead of a DERP server.
• Costs battery and data: other devices' connections pass through this phone — best on Wi-Fi and charging.
• Used only where the tailnet's access policy grants relay use to this device (tailscale.com/cap/relay); the visual policy editor in the admin console can add that grant.
• On mobile data or behind carrier NAT other devices can rarely reach the phone; a fixed port forwarded on the router helps.
• The official Tailscale app for Android cannot do this; TailSocks runs its own daemon, which can. The coordination server can still turn it off for this device — this row then says so.
The coordination server has turned the relay off for this device
Empty or 0: any free port, a new one on every start. Choose a fixed port to forward it on the router.
Not a UDP port: use a number from 0 to 65535.

Send the traffic the tailnet routes through app connectors (SaaS apps, sites that admit only known addresses) out through this phone\'s internet connection.\n• Needs a tag on this device and an app connector for that tag in the admin console (Apps), with access rules that allow it.\n• Costs battery and data: that traffic goes out through this phone.
A node joins only once a trusted device signs its key. Open for this device\'s key and the nodes waiting for a signature.
On · this device is locked out

With Tailnet Lock on, a node joins the tailnet only once a device with a trusted key signs it — the coordination server alone cannot add one. This screen shows the lock as this device sees it, and on a device with a trusted key it signs nodes that are waiting. Turning the lock on, adding and removing trusted keys is done with the CLI on a trusted device.
Connect to see Tailnet Lock\'s status.

Nothing is checked: the coordination server alone decides who joins. It is turned on from a trusted device with “tailscale lock init”, which needs this device\'s key below if this phone is to sign nodes too.
Holds a trusted key: it can sign nodes
Signed: it is in the tailnet
Not signed: cut off from the tailnet until a trusted device signs it
No key yet: it appears once this profile has logged in
Add it as a trusted key (“tailscale lock add …” on a trusted device) to sign nodes from this phone. Tap to copy.
Run it on a device with a trusted key to let this phone in. Tap to copy.
